lessons.title: Study Session 1: Setting Up a Business Profile and Catalog

blocks.text: Introduction Immaculate Nabirye bakes cakes and pastries from Masaka and had left her WhatsApp Business profile almost entirely blank, no listed hours, no address, no catalog, describing each item by typed message whenever a customer asked, until a first-time visitor to the profile messaged to ask whether the business was even real, since nothing on the page itself confirmed it. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about the factors that build consumer trust in direct WhatsApp transactions. Distinguish an incomplete business profile from one that gives a customer confidence to buy. Apply a method for building a complete WhatsApp Business profile and catalog. Recognise which profile and catalog elements matter most for a first-time customer's trust. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 A Profile That Looked Abandoned Immaculate Nabirye's WhatsApp Business account had no business hours listed, no address, no catalog, and only a generic default photo, with every product described one at a time by typed message whenever someone asked. A first-time customer, browsing before deciding whether to trust the account with an order, messaged to ask whether the business was even real, since nothing visible on the profile itself confirmed that it was. 2.2 What Research Found About Trust in Direct WhatsApp Transactions Lydia Kharis Luis and Regi Sanjaya studied the factors building consumer trust in direct transactions via WhatsApp for a 2025 case study of an online thrift shop. Seller responsiveness, transparency of information and the ease of the payment process were identified as the specific factors that built consumer trust in a WhatsApp transaction, with an incomplete or generic profile leaving that transparency largely unmet before a conversation even began. 2.3 Building a Complete Profile and Catalog Filling In Every Business Profile Field Completing the business name, address, hours, description and category fields WhatsApp Business actually provides, rather than leaving the defaults in place, gives a first-time visitor the basic confirmation that a real, findable business is on the other end of the chat. Building a Catalog Customers Can Browse Without Asking Adding products to the catalog feature directly, each with its own photo, price and description, replaces one-off typed answers with something a customer can browse and trust before ever sending a message. 2.4 Key Practices Complete every business profile field WhatsApp Business provides, including hours and address. Add each product to the catalog with its own photo, price and description. Keep catalog prices and descriptions current as they change. Review the profile periodically as though seeing it for the first time. 2.5 A Worked Example: Immaculate's Rebuilt Profile Immaculate filled in her business hours, address and a description of her bakery, then built a full catalog of her twelve regular items, each with its own photo and price, replacing the habit of describing every cake individually whenever a customer happened to ask. Immaculate's baking itself had never been in question among customers who already knew her personally. What a first-time visitor saw on opening the profile was closer to an empty shell than a working bakery, and only filling in that profile and building the catalog ever gave a stranger a reason to trust what they could not yet taste for themselves. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Leaving a business profile's default fields blank gives a first-time customer nothing to confirm the business is real before they are asked to trust it with a purchase, precisely the gap in Immaculate's original profile. Answering catalog questions one at a time by typed message, rather than building a catalog customers can browse directly, puts unnecessary weight on a seller's responsiveness alone to carry a customer's trust. 2.7 A Profile Speaks Before a Seller Ever Does Immaculate's cakes had a strong local reputation among people who already knew her personally. A stranger arriving at the profile for the first time had no way to see that reputation directly, and only a complete profile and catalog ever gave that stranger the same starting confidence an existing customer already carried in. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to build a complete WhatsApp Business profile and catalog that gives a customer reason to trust the business. Study Session 2 turns from building the profile to organizing the conversations that follow once customers start using it.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own WhatsApp Business profile. Would a first-time visitor be able to confirm the business is real without messaging first? 2. Complete every profile field on a real WhatsApp Business account and build a catalog entry for at least three products. Practical Output: Practical Output A completed WhatsApp Business profile and a catalog of at least three real products, each with its own photo, price and description. 7.0 References and Further Reading Luis, L.K., & Sanjaya, R. (2025). Analysis of consumer trust in direct transaction methods via WhatsApp in "Take on Thrift" online shop. Dinasti International Journal of Economics, Finance & Accounting, 6(3), 2018 to 2023. Optional further reading, curriculum-team reviewed: Zechariah 8:16, on speaking every man the truth to his neighbour, and executing judgment of truth and peace in the gates. Qur'an, Surah Al-Baqarah 2:42, on not mixing truth with falsehood, nor concealing the truth while knowing it.
Evidence to keep Keep a written note, worksheet, reflection or practical output from this study session. Your progress should show real learning before the quiz.

lessons.title: Study Session 2: Organizing Conversations with Labels

blocks.text: Introduction Abena Frimpong has run her kente cloth business by herself in the three years since she was widowed, and had let every customer conversation sit in one long, undifferentiated chat list, until a paid order sat unfulfilled for two weeks among dozens of unrelated browsing questions, discovered only when the customer asked, publicly in a status comment, where the order had gone. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about the effect of categorizing incoming customer messages as volume grows. Distinguish an undifferentiated chat list from one organized by label. Apply a method for using WhatsApp's label system to track customer and order status. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 An Order Lost Among Dozens of Questions Abena Frimpong's chat list held every conversation exactly as it arrived, browsing questions, price checks and paid orders all sitting side by side with nothing to tell them apart. A paid order sat unfulfilled for two weeks, buried among dozens of unrelated browsing questions, until the customer asked publicly, in a status comment visible to Abena's other followers, where her order had gone. 2.2 What Research Found About Categorizing Customer Messages C.S. Kanimozhi Selvi, S. Jyothi Shri, R. Prasshanthini, Neelamegan and R. Sanjay built and evaluated a system for automatically categorizing and prioritizing customer support messages for a 2025 conference study. Manual, uncategorized handling of a growing volume of customer messages was found to be time-consuming and prone to error, while systematically categorizing incoming messages measurably improved how efficiently they were handled. 2.3 Organizing Conversations by Label Creating Labels That Match Real Order Stages Creating a small set of labels that match the actual stages a conversation moves through, such as new enquiry, paid order and completed order, marks each chat with a status a busy seller can spot in passing, instead of leaving it identical to every other chat in the list. Applying and Updating a Label the Moment Status Changes Applying the correct label the moment a conversation's status actually changes, rather than at the end of a busy day, keeps the label list an accurate picture of what still needs attention instead of a record of what used to be true. 2.4 Key Practices Create a small set of labels matching the real stages a conversation moves through. Apply or update a label the moment a conversation's status changes. Review the paid order label specifically at least once a day. 2.5 A Worked Example: Abena's Labeled Chat List Abena created four labels, new enquiry, quote sent, paid order and completed, and went back through her current chats applying the correct one to each, then made a habit of updating a chat's label the moment its status changed rather than waiting until the end of the day. Abena's individual replies had never been the problem; she answered every message she saw promptly and courteously. A paid order carried no visible marker distinguishing it from a passing question, and only labeling conversations by their real status ever let a busy chat list show, at a glance, which orders still needed her attention. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Leaving every conversation in one undifferentiated list, with no marker separating a paid order from a browsing question, lets a genuine order disappear into ordinary message volume, exactly what produced Abena's two-week gap. Applying a label only at the end of a busy day, rather than the moment status actually changes, leaves the label list describing what used to be true rather than what needs attention right now. 2.7 A Chat List Only Shows What It Is Told to Show Abena's kente business had never lacked genuine customers ready to buy. What her chat list lacked was any way to tell a paid order apart from an ordinary question at a glance, and only a working label system ever gave a busy list that visible difference. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to organize conversations with labels that track customer and order status. Study Session 3 turns from organizing conversations to answering the questions inside them faster.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own chat list. Could a paid order sit unnoticed among ordinary questions the way Abena's did? 2. Create a small set of labels for one real WhatsApp Business account and apply them to every current conversation. Practical Output: Practical Output A labeled chat list for one real WhatsApp Business account, with labels matching real conversation stages applied to every current conversation. 7.0 References and Further Reading Selvi, C.S.K., Shri, S.J., Prasshanthini, R., Neelamegan, & Sanjay, R. (2025). Customer support ticket categorization and prioritization using natural language processing. Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Futuristic Technology (INCOFT 2025), 3, 690 to 698. Optional further reading, curriculum-team reviewed: Exodus 18:25, on Moses choosing able men out of all Israel and making them heads over the people. Qur'an, Surah An-Naml 27:17, on Solomon's soldiers being gathered before him, marshalled in ranks.

lessons.title: Study Session 3: Using Quick Replies to Answer Common Questions Fast

blocks.text: Introduction Mulenga Chanda sells mobile phone accessories from Solwezi, and had been typing out fresh answers to the same handful of questions, price, availability, delivery time, by hand every single time a customer asked, until a review of a month's chat history showed he had typed some version of the same four answers well over two hundred times. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about how waiting shapes a customer's behaviour during a text-based service conversation. Distinguish a business retyping the same answer repeatedly from one using saved quick replies. Apply a method for building and using a set of quick replies for common questions. Recognise which questions are frequent enough to justify a quick reply. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 The Same Four Answers, Typed Out Two Hundred Times Mulenga Chanda answered every customer question by typing a fresh reply, even when the question, price, availability or delivery time, was one he had already answered many times that same week. Reviewing a month of his own chat history, he counted well over two hundred instances of retyping some close variation of the same four answers, each one composed again from scratch. 2.2 What Research Found About Waiting in Text-Based Service Noyan Ilk and Guohou Shang examined how waiting shaped customer behaviour using operational data from a live-chat contact center for a 2022 study. Waiting time was found to measurably shape how a customer engaged for the remainder of the conversation, evidence that the time a customer spends waiting for a reply is not a neutral pause but an active part of the service experience itself. 2.3 Building and Using Quick Replies Saving a Quick Reply for Every Genuinely Common Question Saving a ready-made quick reply for each question that comes up often enough to recognise on sight, price, availability, delivery time, replaces retyping the same answer with selecting it in a few taps. Personalizing a Quick Reply Before Sending It Adding a customer's name or a small specific detail to a quick reply before sending it keeps the speed of a saved answer from reading as an obviously automated, impersonal one. 2.4 Key Practices Save a quick reply for every question that comes up often enough to recognise on sight. Personalize a quick reply with a specific detail before sending it. Review chat history periodically to catch a new question worth saving. Retire a quick reply once the information it contains is no longer accurate. 2.5 A Worked Example: Mulenga's Saved Quick Replies Mulenga built four quick replies covering price, availability, delivery time and payment options, each written to be personalized with a customer's name and the specific product asked about before sending, and began using them for every question that matched. Mulenga's answers themselves had never been wrong; every typed reply gave a customer accurate, honest information. Retyping the same answer from scratch each time cost minutes that a saved, personalized reply did not need to spend, and only building that set of quick replies ever gave Mulenga back the time two hundred repeated answers had quietly taken from his week. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Retyping the same answer from scratch every time a familiar question arrives costs real time across dozens of repeated questions, exactly the pattern behind Mulenga's two hundred retyped replies. Sending a quick reply with no personal detail added risks a customer feeling handled by a script rather than answered by a person. 2.7 Speed and Personal Attention Are Not Actually a Trade-Off Mulenga had always intended every customer to feel personally attended to, and typing each answer by hand had felt, to him, like the surest way to guarantee that. A saved, personalized quick reply gave a customer the same individual attention in a fraction of the time, and only building that set of replies ever showed him speed and personal attention could sit inside the very same message. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to build and use quick replies that answer common questions fast without losing a personal touch. Study Session 4 turns from answering questions quickly during the day to what a customer sees when no one is available to answer at all.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own repeated questions. Which ones come up often enough to justify a saved quick reply? 2. Build at least three quick replies for one real WhatsApp Business account, each written to be personalized before sending. Practical Output: Practical Output A set of at least three quick replies for one real WhatsApp Business account, each written to be personalized with a customer's name or a specific detail. 7.0 References and Further Reading Ilk, N., & Shang, G. (2022). The impact of waiting on customer-instigated service time: Field evidence from a live-chat contact center. Journal of Operations Management, 68(5), 447 to 471. Optional further reading, curriculum-team reviewed: Isaiah 50:4, on the tongue of the learned, to know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary. Qur'an, Surah Aal-Imran 3:133, on hastening to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth.

lessons.title: Study Session 4: Automating Greeting and Away Messages to Set Clear Expectations

blocks.text: Introduction Josué Mwamba works another job during the day and only replies to his leather sandal business's messages in the evening, and had left the automated greeting and away message features turned off entirely, so a customer messaging at midday received no reply of any kind, and no signal that a reply was coming at all, until she messaged a competing seller instead and later mentioned why. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about how a stated waiting-time guarantee shapes a customer's satisfaction with a wait. Distinguish silence with no signal of a reply from an honest, specific expectation about when one will come. Apply a method for configuring automated greeting and away messages that set a clear, honest expectation. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 Silence With No Signal a Reply Was Coming Josué Mwamba's leather sandal business had its automated greeting and away messages turned off entirely, so a message sent while he was at his day job received nothing back at all, not even an automatic acknowledgment, until he returned home that evening. A customer who messaged at midday, heard nothing for hours, and eventually messaged a competing seller instead later mentioned, almost in passing, that the silence itself was what had pushed her to look elsewhere. 2.2 What Research Found About Waiting-Time Guarantees Piyush Kumar, Manohar U. Kalwani and Maqbool Dada studied how an explicit waiting-time guarantee shaped customer satisfaction with a wait for a 1997 study. Customers given a specific, honest guarantee about how long a wait would last reported more positive satisfaction with that wait than customers given no stated expectation at all, provided the guarantee was actually met. 2.3 Configuring Automated Messages That Set a Clear Expectation Writing an Away Message With a Specific, Honest Reply Window Writing an away message that states a specific, realistic window for a reply, such as by this evening, rather than a vague apology or no message at all, gives a waiting customer the same kind of guarantee that measurably improves satisfaction with a wait. Setting Business Hours So the Away Message Triggers Automatically Setting accurate business hours so the away message triggers on its own outside them, rather than depending on Josué remembering to switch it on manually, keeps the expectation reliable even on a day he forgets to think about the account at all. 2.4 Key Practices Write an away message that states a specific, realistic window for a reply. Set accurate business hours so the away message triggers automatically. Confirm the greeting and away messages are actually turned on, not just written. 2.5 A Worked Example: Josué's Configured Away Message Josué wrote an away message stating plainly that messages received outside nine in the morning to six in the evening would be answered by the following morning at the latest, set his business hours to match his actual day job schedule, and turned the feature on for the first time since opening the account. Josué's evening replies had always come, without fail, once he actually sat down to answer messages. A customer messaging during the day had no way to know that reply was coming at all, and only an honest, specific away message ever gave a daytime customer the same guarantee his evening customers had already come to rely on over time. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Leaving automated greeting and away messages turned off entirely gives a customer no signal a reply is coming at all, precisely what pushed Josué's midday customer toward a competitor. Writing a vague away message with no specific reply window still leaves a customer guessing, even though something was technically sent. 2.7 A Guarantee Kept Is Worth More Than Silence Explained Later Josué's sandals and his evening responsiveness had never been the actual problem; every message he saw in the evening received a full, careful reply. A customer messaging during the day had no way to know that evening reply was coming, and only a specific, automatically triggered away message ever gave a daytime customer the same confidence his evening customers already had. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to configure automated greeting and away messages that set a clear, honest expectation for when a reply will come. Study Session 5 turns from replying to individual customers to reaching many customers at once, responsibly.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own away message, if you have one. Does it state a specific window for a reply, or leave a customer guessing? 2. Write an away message with a specific reply window for one real WhatsApp Business account, and set business hours so it triggers automatically. Practical Output: Practical Output A configured away message with a specific reply window and accurate business hours for one real WhatsApp Business account. 7.0 References and Further Reading Kumar, P., Kalwani, M.U., & Dada, M. (1997). The impact of waiting time guarantees on customers' waiting experiences. Marketing Science, 16(4), 295 to 314. Optional further reading, curriculum-team reviewed: Numbers 30:2, on a man who vows a vow, or swears an oath, not breaking his word but doing according to all that proceeds out of his mouth. Qur'an, Surah As-Saff 61:3, on it being greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do.

lessons.title: Study Session 5: Using Broadcast Lists to Reach Customers Responsibly

blocks.text: Introduction Voahangy Rakoto looks after her elderly mother's daily needs in between the hours she gives to her vanilla and spice business in Antsirabe, and had added every phone number from every past order into a single broadcast list without asking, sending a weekly product update to all of them regardless of whether they had ever agreed to receive it, until enough recipients blocked the number that WhatsApp itself restricted the account's ability to send messages at all. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about the role of consumer permission in mobile messaging advertising effectiveness. Distinguish a broadcast list built from opted-in customers from one built from every past contact. Apply a method for building and using a broadcast list responsibly. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 Added Without Asking, Blocked Without Warning Voahangy Rakoto added every phone number from every past order, whether from a single tiny purchase or a large recurring one, into a single broadcast list, sending a weekly update to the entire list regardless of whether any individual recipient had ever agreed to receive it. Enough recipients blocked the number over several months that WhatsApp itself restricted the account's ability to send further messages, a restriction that arrived with no individual warning either. 2.2 What Research Found About Permission in Mobile Messaging Fatim Bamba and Stuart J. Barnes studied the role of consumer permission in the effectiveness of mobile messaging advertising for a 2007 study. Permission was found to be a significant factor shaping how a consumer received and responded to a message, meaning a message sent without a recipient's prior agreement carried real risk regardless of how genuinely useful its content actually was. 2.3 Building and Using a Broadcast List Responsibly Adding a Customer to a Broadcast List Only With Clear Agreement Adding a customer to a broadcast list only after they clearly agree to receive it, rather than by default from a past order, keeps the list limited to people who actually want the messages it sends. Making It Simple for Anyone to Leave the List Making it clear and simple for anyone to ask to be removed from a broadcast list, and acting on that request promptly, keeps the list trustworthy and reduces the chance of a recipient blocking the number instead of just asking to stop. 2.4 Key Practices Add a customer to a broadcast list only after they clearly agree to receive it. Make it simple for anyone to ask to leave the list, and act on that request promptly. Keep broadcast messages limited to content the list actually agreed to receive. 2.5 A Worked Example: Voahangy's Rebuilt List Voahangy cleared her existing broadcast list entirely and rebuilt it by messaging past customers individually to ask whether they wanted to keep receiving weekly updates, adding only those who said yes, and included a simple line in every future broadcast explaining how to leave the list at any time. Voahangy's weekly updates had always contained real, useful information about new spice harvests and prices. Nothing about a customer's single past order had ever meant they wanted that update landing in their chat every week without being asked, and only rebuilding the list around actual agreement ever protected the account from the same restriction happening a second time. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Adding every past contact to a broadcast list by default, without asking, treats a single past purchase as permission for ongoing messages a customer never actually agreed to receive, exactly what led to Voahangy's restricted account. Making it difficult or unclear how to leave a broadcast list pushes a frustrated recipient toward blocking the number entirely instead of simply asking to stop. 2.7 Reach Without Permission Eventually Costs the Reach Itself Voahangy's vanilla and spices had never been the reason recipients blocked her number; the content of her updates was genuinely useful to people who actually wanted it. What was missing was any real agreement behind who received those updates, and only building the list around actual permission ever protected her ability to reach anyone at all. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to build and use a broadcast list that reaches customers who have actually agreed to receive it. Study Session 6 closes this course by turning to what happens once a single-device account and a growing team stop fitting together.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own broadcast list, if you have one. Did every recipient actually agree to be on it? 2. Rebuild a broadcast list for one real WhatsApp Business account so it includes only customers who have clearly agreed to receive it. Practical Output: Practical Output A rebuilt broadcast list for one real WhatsApp Business account, including only customers who have clearly agreed to receive it, with a stated way to leave the list. 7.0 References and Further Reading Bamba, F., & Barnes, S.J. (2007). SMS advertising, permission and the consumer: A study. Business Process Management Journal, 13(6), 815 to 829. Optional further reading, curriculum-team reviewed: Proverbs 25:17, on seldom setting foot in a neighbour's house, lest they have their fill and come to hate it. Qur'an, Surah An-Nur 24:28, on not entering houses if no one is found therein until permission is given.

lessons.title: Study Session 6: Choosing Between the App and the Business API as a Team Grows

blocks.text: Introduction Sipho Dlamini sells handwoven mats and textiles from Malkerns, and had grown the business to the point where three family members were all trying to answer messages from the same single WhatsApp Business App account on one shared phone, with no way to see who had already replied to a given customer, until two of them sent two different delivery estimates to the same question within minutes of each other. 1.0 Learning Outcomes By the end of this study session, you should be able to: Explain what research found about the effect of adopting the WhatsApp Business API for a growing small business. Distinguish the single-device App's limits from what the multi-agent Business API actually provides. Apply a method for deciding whether and when to move from the App to the Business API. 2.0 Main Content 2.1 Two Different Answers to the Same Question Sipho Dlamini's mat and textile business had grown to the point where three family members all tried to answer customer messages from the single WhatsApp Business App account, installed on one shared phone, with no way for any of them to see whether someone else had already replied to a given conversation. Two family members answered the same customer's question within minutes of each other, giving two different delivery estimates and leaving the customer, and both of them, confused about which answer to trust. 2.2 What Research Found About Adopting the Business API Hassan Mustafa and six co-authors examined the impact of adopting the WhatsApp Business API in a case study of ninety-eight small businesses in Dubai for a 2023 study. Adopting the Business API was found to improve operational efficiency and specifically the ability to handle multiple customer conversations at once through a shared team inbox, a capability the single-device App does not provide. 2.3 Deciding Whether and When to Move to the Business API Recognising When One Device Stops Being Enough Noticing specific signs, such as two people answering the same conversation differently, or messages sitting unanswered because no one realised they were unclaimed, signals that a single shared device has reached its real limit rather than simply needing better habits. Weighing the Business API's Setup Cost Against the Team's Actual Size Weighing the Business API's greater setup complexity and cost against the team's actual number of people and message volume, rather than moving to it purely because the option exists, keeps the decision matched to the business's real current size. 2.4 Key Practices Watch for two people answering the same conversation differently as a sign the App has reached its limit. Weigh the Business API's setup cost and complexity against the team's actual size and volume. Assign clear conversation ownership if staying on the App a while longer. 2.5 A Worked Example: Sipho's Move to the Business API After the second instance of two family members giving conflicting answers to the same customer, Sipho researched the Business API's shared team inbox feature, weighed its setup cost against the business's now-genuine three-person team, and moved the account over, giving each family member their own login tied to the same shared conversation history. Sipho's family had never lacked the care or attention to answer a customer well individually; each of the three answered every message they personally saw responsibly. The single shared device gave none of them visibility into what the others had already answered, and only moving to a platform built for more than one person at once ever removed the confusion two honest answers to the same question had been causing. 2.6 Common Pitfalls Staying on the single-device App well past the point where more than one person needs to answer messages leaves conversations invisible between team members, exactly the gap that produced Sipho's two conflicting answers. Moving to the Business API before a team's actual size or volume justifies its added setup cost and complexity can add overhead a smaller operation does not yet need. 2.7 The Right Tool Matches the Size of the Team Using It Sipho's mats and textiles had built a growing customer base well before the API move, and nothing about the products themselves had caused the confusion. The single shared device had reached the point where more than one person needed visibility into the same conversation, and only a platform built for a team, rather than a single device, ever gave that visibility back. 3.0 Study Session Summary and Conclusion In this study session, you learned to decide whether and when to move from the WhatsApp Business App to the Business API as a team grows. This closes Course 101 and prepares you for Course 102, Instagram and Facebook Shop Integration for Small Enterprises, the next course in Pathway 62.

Reflect and Grow — Self-Assessment 1. Think about your own team, if more than one person answers messages. Could two people give a customer two different answers without either of you knowing? 2. Assess whether one real WhatsApp Business account has outgrown the App, and outline what moving to the Business API would involve. Practical Output: Practical Output A written assessment of whether one real WhatsApp Business account has outgrown the single-device App, with a plan for moving to the Business API if warranted. 7.0 References and Further Reading Mustafa, H., Al-Tkhayneh, K.M., Imtiaz, R., Hadi, S.A., Al Qaruty, R., Abokhoza, R., & Ellala, Z.K. (2023). The impact of using WhatsApp Business (API) in marketing for small business. Proceedings of the 2023 Tenth International Conference on Social Networks Analysis, Management and Security (SNAMS), 1 to 6. Qur'an, Surah Aal-Imran 3:103, on holding firmly to the rope of Allah together and not becoming divided.

quiz.q: A customer messaged Josué's business at midday and heard nothing until evening, with no automated acknowledgment at all. What did this reveal?
options: Josué's sandals had not actually been worth buying
Leaving automated away messages turned off entirely gives a customer no signal a reply is coming at all
Leather sandals should not be sold through WhatsApp
Josué had been pricing his sandals too high
quiz.explain: Review Study Session 4 (Automating Greeting and Away Messages to Set Clear Expectations) before continuing.

quiz.q: According to Kumar, Kalwani and Dada's 1997 study, how did customers respond to a stated waiting-time guarantee?
options: They reported more positive satisfaction with a wait than customers given no stated expectation, provided the guarantee was met
They reported no difference in satisfaction regardless of any guarantee
They reported less satisfaction than customers given no guarantee at all
Waiting-time guarantees were found to have no measurable effect
quiz.explain: Review Study Session 4 (Automating Greeting and Away Messages to Set Clear Expectations) before continuing.

quiz.q: What does this session recommend an away message state?
options: Nothing beyond a generic apology
A specific, realistic window for when a reply will come
The business's full product catalog
A request for the customer to call instead

quiz.q: Enough recipients blocked Voahangy's number that WhatsApp restricted her account's ability to send messages. What did this reveal?
options: Voahangy's spice business had never attracted genuine customers
Adding every past contact to a broadcast list without asking treats a single purchase as permission a customer never actually gave
Broadcast lists should never be used by small businesses
Voahangy had been overpricing her vanilla and spices

quiz.q: According to Bamba and Barnes's 2007 study, what did consumer permission significantly shape?

Only the price a consumer was willing to pay
Nothing measurable about mobile messaging effectiveness
The consumer's preference for one delivery method over another
quiz.explain: Review Study Session 5 (Using Broadcast Lists to Reach Customers Responsibly) before continuing.

quiz.q: What does this session recommend before adding a customer to a broadcast list?
options: Nothing; every past contact should be added automatically

A minimum purchase amount
A formal written contract
